tasks.title: Runtime via Builder
tasks.statement:
In a plain fn main build a multi-threaded runtime: Builder::new_multi_thread() with 2 worker threads, the thread name "worker" (thread_name("worker")) and enable_all(). Use block_on to run a spawn task that prints "name starts with worker: true" (checking std::thread::current().name()).

Expected output:
`name starts with worker: true`
tasks.hint: Builder::new_multi_thread().worker_threads(2).thread_name("worker").enable_all().build().

tasks.title: Single-threaded runtime
tasks.statement:
Use #[tokio::main(flavor = "current_thread")]. Start 5 spawn tasks, each returning the thread id (std::thread::current().id()) as a string; check that there is only one thread and that it is the same as the main thread: "threads: 1".

Expected output:
`threads: 1`
tasks.hint: current_thread: everything runs on one thread.

tasks.title: Handle from a plain thread
tasks.statement:
Inside #[tokio::main] get Handle::current() and pass it to std::thread::spawn; the thread uses handle.spawn to start an async task (sleep 10 ms, returns 99) and sends the result back through std::sync::mpsc. Print «99».

Expected output:
99
tasks.hint: A Handle can be passed to another thread and used for spawn and block_on.

tasks.title: block_on twice
tasks.statement:
In a plain main create one Runtime and call block_on twice: first put a value into a shared Arc<Mutex<Vec<u32>>> from a task, then the second block_on reads it. Print «[1, 2]».

Expected output:
[1, 2]
tasks.hint: One Runtime can be used for several block_on calls.

tasks.title: Values from tasks
tasks.statement:
Start three spawn tasks returning the String «a», the Vec<u32> [1, 2] and the tuple (3, true). Wait for them with tokio::join! and print one line each: «a», «[1, 2]», «(3, true)».

Expected output:
a
[1, 2]
(3, true)
tasks.hint: join! over JoinHandle returns a tuple of Results.

tasks.title: abort and is_finished
tasks.statement:
Start a task that sleeps for 1 s; immediately check is_finished() (false), call abort(), await it and print: «false», «cancelled: true», then is_finished() — «true».

Expected output:
false
cancelled: true
tasks.hint: abort() interrupts at the nearest .await; awaiting the handle returns a JoinError with is_cancelled.

tasks.title: A panic and its message
tasks.statement:
Start a task that panics with panic!("boom"). Extract the message: JoinError::into_panic() gives a Box<dyn Any + Send>; cast it to &str (downcast_ref::<&str>()). Print "panic: boom".

Expected output:
`panic: boom`
tasks.hint: into_panic() returns the panic payload.

tasks.title: JoinSet and indexes
tasks.statement:
Start 6 tasks in a JoinSet; task i sleeps (6 − i)·5 ms and returns (i, i·i). Collect the results and print them sorted by i: [(0, 0), (1, 1), (2, 4), (3, 9), (4, 16), (5, 25)].

Expected output:
[(0, 0), (1, 1), (2, 4), (3, 9), (4, 16), (5, 25)]
tasks.hint: Results arrive in completion order — sort by index.

tasks.title: abort_all
tasks.statement:
Start 4 endless tasks (sleep 1 s) in a JoinSet, call abort_all() and wait for all of them with join_next: count the is_cancelled errors. Print "cancelled: 4".

Expected output:
`cancelled: 4`
tasks.hint: After abort_all, join_next returns Err(cancelled) for each task.

tasks.title: Dropping the set cancels tasks
tasks.statement:
A task holds a Guard that increments a shared AtomicUsize in Drop. Start 3 such tasks (sleep 1 s) in a JoinSet, let them start (sleep 10 ms), drop the set and give time for cleanup (sleep 20 ms). Print "cleared: 3".

Expected output:
`cleared: 3`
tasks.hint: Drop for JoinSet calls abort_all.

tasks.title: Blocking tasks run in parallel
tasks.statement:
Start 4 spawn_blocking tasks, each sleeping (std::thread::sleep) for 100 ms. Wait for all of them and check that the total time is under 300 ms: "in parallel: true".

Expected output:
`in parallel: true`
tasks.hint: The blocking thread pool runs the tasks at the same time.

tasks.title: block_in_place
tasks.statement:
On the multi-threaded runtime, inside a task (spawn), call block_in_place to compute the sum of squares 1..=1000 (u64) and return it: «333833500».

Expected output:
333833500
tasks.hint: block_in_place is allowed only on multi_thread.

tasks.title: LocalSet and Rc
tasks.statement:
On current_thread create a LocalSet; inside run_until start 5 spawn_local tasks, each adding its own number (1…5) to an Rc<RefCell<u32>> and doing nothing after yield_now. Wait for all of them and print «15».

Expected output:
15
tasks.hint: spawn_local accepts !Send futures inside a LocalSet.

tasks.title: task_local!
tasks.statement:
Declare tokio::task_local! { static REQ_ID: u32; }. Start two tasks: one with REQ_ID.scope(1, …), the other with scope(2, …); each calls a shared async fn log() -> String that returns "request <id>" from REQ_ID.get(). Print both results: "request 1", "request 2".

Expected output:
`request 1`
`request 2`
tasks.hint: REQ_ID.scope(value, future) provides the value while the future runs.

tasks.title: Task ids
tasks.statement:
Start 5 tasks, each returning tokio::task::id(). Check that all the ids are different (main is not a task, so it has no id to compare with): print "unique: 5".

Expected output:
`unique: 5`
tasks.hint: tokio::task::id() returns an Id that implements Hash.

tasks.title: Fairness
tasks.statement:
On current_thread start a "busy" task: while !flag { yield_now().await }, and a second one that raises the flag (AtomicBool) right away. Wait for both and print "flag raised". (Without yield_now the task would hang.)

Expected output:
`flag raised`
tasks.hint: yield_now hands control to other tasks on the same thread.

tasks.title: Detaching
tasks.statement:
Drop the JoinHandle right after spawn and make sure the task keeps running: after 10 ms it sends "alive" through a oneshot. Print "alive".

Expected output:
`alive`
tasks.hint: Dropping a JoinHandle does not cancel the task.

tasks.title: Dropping the runtime
tasks.statement:
In a plain main create a Runtime and spawn a task with a Guard (Drop increments an AtomicUsize) that sleeps for 10 s. Let it start (block_on sleep 10 ms), then drop(rt). Print the number of Drops that ran: «1».

Expected output:
1
tasks.hint: When a runtime is dropped, its tasks are cancelled and their destructors run.

tasks.title: shutdown_timeout
tasks.statement:
Start a 50 ms spawn_blocking in the runtime (std sleep) and call rt.shutdown_timeout(Duration::from_secs(2)); print "runtime stopped" and "faster than 2 s: true".

Expected output:
`runtime stopped`
`faster than 2 s: true`
tasks.hint: shutdown_timeout waits for blocking tasks no longer than the limit.

tasks.title: Handle::try_current
tasks.statement:
Show that Handle::try_current() outside a runtime returns Err (print "outside: false") and inside it returns Ok ("inside: true"). First call it in a plain main before creating the runtime, then inside block_on.

Expected output:
`outside: false`
`inside: true`
tasks.hint: try_current does not panic: it returns a Result.

tasks.title: Parallel map
tasks.statement:
Write async fn par_map(items: Vec<u32>, f: fn(u32) -> u32) -> Vec<u32>: each item is processed in its own spawn_blocking task; the result is in input order. For f = |x| x * x and items 1..=8 print [1, 4, 9, 16, 25, 36, 49, 64].

Expected output:
[1, 4, 9, 16, 25, 36, 49, 64]
tasks.hint: Await the handles in launch order to keep the order.

tasks.title: Many tasks
tasks.statement:
Start 20000 spawn tasks, each incrementing a shared AtomicUsize; wait for all of them (JoinSet) and print «20000».

Expected output:
20000
tasks.hint: Tokio tasks are very cheap: tens of thousands are no problem.

tasks.title: Fan-out and fan-in
tasks.statement:
Fan-out/fan-in: 4 workers (spawn), each processes its own quarter of the numbers 1..=100 (a sum) and sends the partial sum into an mpsc channel; main adds up the 4 values received: «5050».

Expected output:
5050
tasks.hint: You need drop(tx) so that recv returns None after the last sender.

tasks.title: Retry with cancellation
tasks.statement:
Write async fn retry<F, Fut>(n: u32, mut f: F) -> Result<u32, String>, where F: FnMut(u32) -> Fut, Fut: Future<Output = Result<u32, String>>: it tries f(attempt) for attempt = 1…n and returns the first Ok or the last error. For an f that succeeds only on the third attempt print "Ok(3)"; for a hopeless one print `Err("failure 3")`.

Expected output:
`Ok(3)`
`Err("failure 3")`
tasks.hint: A loop over the attempts; return early on Ok.

tasks.title: Result from tasks
tasks.statement:
Write async fn run_all(n: u32) -> Result<Vec<u32>, tokio::task::JoinError>: start n tasks (i·10) and collect the results using ? on the handles; for n = 4 print «Ok([0, 10, 20, 30])».

Expected output:
Ok([0, 10, 20, 30])
tasks.hint: JoinError implements Error: the ? operator works.

tasks.title: abort on a blocking task
tasks.statement:
Show that abort() does not stop a spawn_blocking task that has already started: the task sets started, sleeps 60 ms and sets done (AtomicBool). Main waits for started (polling with a 1 ms sleep), calls abort(), waits 100 ms and prints "flag: true".

Expected output:
`flag: true`
tasks.hint: The blocking thread runs to the end: cancellation applies only to tasks that have not started yet.

tasks.title: Worker pool
tasks.statement:
A pool of 3 workers reads jobs (the numbers 1…12) from a shared mpsc channel (Arc<tokio::sync::Mutex<Receiver<u32>>>), and each adds the square of its number to a shared AtomicU64. The sender is closed, main waits for the workers (JoinSet) and prints «650».

Expected output:
650
tasks.hint: The receiver is shared: wrap it in Arc<Mutex<…>>; None is the signal to finish.

tasks.title: timeout over a JoinHandle
tasks.statement:
Wrap a task's JoinHandle (sleep 200 ms) in tokio::time::timeout(30 ms): print "timeout"; the task keeps running meanwhile — check through a oneshot that it did finish after 250 ms: "task survived".

Expected output:
`timeout`
`task survived`
tasks.hint: timeout drops the wait on the handle, not the task itself.

tasks.title: How many threads
tasks.statement:
Build a multi-threaded runtime with worker_threads(3) and start 50 spawn tasks, each returning the name of its thread (after a short 1 ms sleep). Print: "threads at most 3: true".

Expected output:
`threads at most 3: true`
tasks.hint: All tasks run on the pool's worker threads.

tasks.title: Fix it: spawn and a reference
tasks.statement:
The program does not compile: the task borrows a local vector. Fix it with Arc so that it prints "sum 10".

Expected output:
`sum 10`
`4`
tasks.hint: Arc::clone and move.
